Talia (platform): Thinking about a lightweight "staged-pointer" activation pattern for on-prem: stage everything, then flip a small activation pointer. Goal: <60s activation window for large model blobs.

Hector (infra): Ok but compatibility is the hard part. Propose a tiny per-snapshot compat-file: {comp, rev, abi_set, min_api, sha}. Run preflight graph check before commit.

Min (ops): Disk-limited sites: we must support stream-activate as fallback. Document tradeoffs: longer activation + higher failure surface. Also need a clear rollback path.

Rae (eng-runtime): Sidecar staging + symlink flip only. Loader must accept dual-paths for a 2-minute grace so in-flight requests don't fail. No in-place lib overwrite.

Ash (sre): Canary plan: leader-elect operator chooses 2-node canary, wait 4m, then rack-level parallel. Operator must snapshot symlink and store a pointer manifest for deterministic rollback.

Talia (platform): Minimal activation metadata: `snapshot=<comp>:<rev>:<sha>:abi=<tag>:signed` stored in operator state. GC unreferenced after default 24h. CLI: `rdu operator prune --dry-run`.

bot-deploy: sandbox run queued: 2024-10-01T02:00Z (ops alerted).

Min (ops): I'll run a dry-run in our isolated lab and post staging/activate/rollback timings + disk metrics.

Rae (eng-runtime): I'll author operator contract (stage/verify/activate/rollback) and a small sequence diagram. Reviewers: @Ash @Hector.

Ash (sre): Also add watchdog timers so a stuck activation auto-rolls back. Metrics to capture: stage_time, activate_window, rollback_time, peak_disk_usage, latency_pct_change.

Talia (platform): Great. I'll turn this into an RFC follow-up and ping reviewers. Thanks.
